title: Activation Functions & Their Gradients
summary: Write ReLU, its backward pass, the tanh-approximated GELU and a numerically stable softmax: the building blocks of every network.

ShapeMismatch.hint: Activations are element-wise (softmax normalizes along one axis), so the output shape must equal the input shape.

NaNInSoftmax.hint: exp() overflows above ~709. Shift the logits by their max along the softmax axis before exponentiating.

hints.test_relu_values: ReLU(x) = max(0, x), element-wise. np.maximum broadcasts the scalar 0.
hints.test_relu_preserves_shape_and_input: Return a new array rather than writing into x.
hints.test_relu_backward: Upstream gradient flows through only where x > 0. Multiply dout by that boolean mask.
hints.test_gelu_asymptotics: For large positive x, GELU ≈ x; for large negative x, GELU ≈ 0.
hints.test_softmax_sums_to_one: Divide by the sum along the chosen axis, with keepdims=True so it broadcasts.
hints.test_softmax_is_numerically_stable: Subtract x.max(axis, keepdims=True) first. Softmax is shift-invariant.
hints.test_softmax_axis: Use the axis argument in both the max and the sum.
hints.test_softmax_invariant_to_shift: If adding a constant changes your output, the normalization is wrong.
